channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Ormond Beach family transforms tennis club in The Trails
item.description: Asaf and Avi Breier are aiming to make Trailside Tennis Club a facility that will develop junior athletes, support longtime players and create a sense of community.

item.title: Flagler County ends conflicts with Flagler Beach over Summertown development
item.description: The Flagler County Commission voted 4-1 to end a conflict resolution process over the Summertown development in Flagler Beach. Commission Kim Carney was the sole vote against it.

item.title: The NASCAR Foundation awards grant to Halifax Health to expand pediatric telemedicine, Child Life Services
item.description: Halifax Health received a total of $450,000 from the NASCAR Foundation.

item.title: Palm Coast to update council's vacancy procedures, borrowing power in November
item.description: 'We need to make sure that the ones we're putting on here are the important ones,' Councilman Ty Miller said. More updates to the charter will be spread out over other elections.

item.title: 227-acre Daytona Beach brush fire near Mosaic neighborhood 100% contained
item.description: The fire, called the Bennet Field Fire, started out 20-25 acres in size west of Mosaic early on Feb. 23.

item.title: Kindergarten readiness lagging in Flagler. It's a community issue, superintendent says
item.description: Many students entering kindergarten are non-verbal, Flagler County Superintendent LaShakia Moore said.

item.title: Letter: Palm Coast mayor: Council approval of East Hampton rezoning request disappointing
item.description: 'The concerns raised by our citizens deserved serious consideration and additional review. Unfortunately, that did not occur.'

item.title: Second annual Masks for Miracles for hospitalized children set for March 21
item.description: 'There's this magic in the air, and people's hearts just open up for the cause,' Organizer Pam Capela said. Funds raised at the event will go to the nonprofit Live Like Cameron.

item.title: Palm Coast Vice Mayor Pontieri on campaign donations and vapes
item.description: Vice Mayor Theresa Carli Pontieri recently announced she would be returning campaign donations from five developers and that she would be co-authoring a bill on smoke shops and vapes.

item.title: Letter: Last-minute East Hampton shift raises concerns
item.description: 'The proposal ... represents a substantial departure from the previously litigated agreement and appears to be structured in a way that sets a precedent for increased density in future developments.'
